leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now — the balance is positive and the squad is at eleven. But the recommended move opens one deliberately, and it should be understood before it is executed rather than discovered afterwards. Winning the auction takes the balance sharply negative from the moment it settles tonight until the unwind sale completes on Sunday afternoon, a window of roughly half a day. That is safe on the stated mechanic: the zero-points penalty bites at matchday start, and the next matchday does not start for another five days, so there is ample room. It is only unsafe if the unwind is forgotten. The buffer left after the unwind is thin but real, and it is not at risk from market movement, because values update once daily and the sale price is therefore locked for the whole window. The one thing that would make this dangerous is bidding any higher: the ceiling is the cash plus that single sale, and there is no second sale available without dropping below eleven players.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is money, not shape. The eleven is full and legal, so there is no formation hole to fix and no penalty exposure. What binds is that Georg is fully invested: the usable ceiling is the cash on hand plus the single sale that a twelve-man squad permits, and that ceiling is what has closed the board to every large name on it. The weakest fielded slots remain the Mainz full-back in defence and the Hamburg midfielder in the middle, and the live trade addresses the second of those.

verdict.detail: One thing needs doing tonight and it has not been done. The raise on the Rohr bid that the last run called for is still not on the board — the offer sitting on him is the old one, and the auction resolves in a little over two hours. This is a Kickbase listing, so highest bid wins outright at expiry and raising buys win probability directly; it is not a manager ask where the seller chooses. The listing still shows Georg as the only bidder, which is exactly the picture Makengo showed eight hours before a rival arrived and took him at the largest premium this league has ever recorded. The next scheduled look lands about twelve minutes before expiry, which is not enough room to react. Everything else on the board is already logged and rejected; the market did not produce a single new opportunity this run.

sell.reason: One sale, and it is strictly conditional on winning the auction. The Hamburg midfielder is the unwind leg: he is the worst points-per-euro body in the squad large enough to fund the purchase, and selling him keeps the shape legal while every alternative either costs more fielded points than the buy adds or is too small to clear the shortfall. The case against him is quality, not availability — he is in his club's probable eleven and absent from the injury table. Two things matter about the timing. If the auction is lost, this sale must not happen at all: the squad would drop below eleven and take the penalty. And if it is won, the sale must wait until after his match on Sunday has finished, or his matchday points are forfeited for nothing. The window this run corrects: his club kick off two hours earlier than the previous run assumed, so the sale window opens earlier and is wider than the ledger previously recorded. It must still close before the evening market-value tick.

buy.reason: The Elversberg defender, and nothing else. He started and scored well in his club's second matchday today — the confirmed team sheet has him in the back four — he is absent from the injury sweep, carries no status flag, and his contract runs long enough that there is no exit risk. On points per euro he is better than every outfielder Georg owns bar three, and swapping him in for the Hamburg midfielder lifts the fielded eleven materially. The premium being asked is set by the affordability ceiling rather than by a judgement that it is enough to win; the contested-Kickbase cluster clears far above it, and that gap cannot be closed without stranding a balance that could not be unwound. Sequencing is not optional: raise first, sell after. A sale before a lost auction leaves ten players and the penalty. Everything else on the board is a logged rejection. The two genuinely new listings since the last run are both injured and both return no points at all — a Dortmund defender whose cruciate ligament injury is confirmed by dated news and matches his status flag, and a Hoffenheim midfielder this ledger had already recorded as an absentee a day before he was listed. The board's expensive names all regressed once their second matchday landed, which made every existing rejection more comfortable rather than less; not one flipped.

standing.name: Maximilian Rohr
standing.why: CONDITIONAL ON THE 2026-09-05T20:00:00Z MARKET-VALUE TICK, WHICH IS 1h13m AWAY AND WILL VERY LIKELY PUT THE LIVE 10.250.000 OFFER UNDERWATER. This does not revise BUY Bsmq4uu (still open, still correct at the current ask); it is the contingency that Bsmq4uu itself asked the next run to price. STATE OF THE OFFER AT 18:45Z: listing prc 9.726.134 = exactly mv, ofc 1 with Georg alone in ofs at 10.250.000 = +5,39%, exs 22363 resolving ~2026-09-06T01:07Z. WHY THE TICK IS THE PROBLEM: Rohr posted ~115 points in MD2 (p 87 -> 202, ap 101) and mvt reads 1 (rising). Every Kickbase listing observed in this ledger carries prc == mv exactly, so the ask moves with the tick. The measured magnitude of a big-matchday tick, taken from this run's own squad sdmvt figures, is +9% to +34%: ter Horst scored 143 and moved +2.244.127 on 8.797.749 = +25,5%; Onyeka scored 139 and moved +2.024.477 on 9.286.468 = +21,8%; Conte scored 106 and moved +1.284.273 on 9.292.405 = +13,8%; Gregoritsch 195 -> +11,8%; Minjae 110 -> +11,8%; Matsima 138 -> +9,0%. Rohr at ~115 sits squarely in that band, so a post-tick mv of roughly 10,7M to 12,2M is the central expectation and +5,39% of headroom does not cover it. THE DECISION RULE, so the 20:45Z run does not re-derive it: re-read list_market at 20:05Z. (a) If the new prc is at or under 10.250.000, do nothing - the standing offer still clears. (b) If the new prc is above 10.250.000 but the affordability ceiling still covers it, RAISE to the ceiling. (c) If the new prc exceeds the ceiling, the buy is DEAD on affordability and the offer should be pulled rather than left to fail. THE CEILING MUST BE RECOMPUTED AT 20:05Z, NOT REUSED FROM HERE - this is the trap in this call. It is cash 1.002.767 plus the single sale a post-buy squad of 12 permits, and BOTH unwind legs move at the same tick in OPPOSITE directions. Lokonga is mvt 2 FALLING with sdmvt -1.125.317 and scored only 44, so his 9.731.816 will probably shrink; Conte is mvt 1 RISING with sdmvt +1.284.273 and scored 106, so his 9.292.405 will probably grow. Take the LARGER of the two post-tick values: selling Lokonga leaves 1/5/2/3 = 5-2-3 fielding 1283, selling Conte leaves 1/5/3/2 = 5-3-2 fielding 1280, a three-point difference that is not worth defending against a cash difference of a million. 10.734.583 recorded here is the PRE-TICK Lokonga-route ceiling and is a placeholder for that computation. WHY RAISING IS RIGHT RATHER THAN MERELY TOLERABLE, WHICH THE HEADLINE PRICE HIDES: the purchase is not P for 101 points, it is (P minus the unwind proceeds) for the NET points gain. Post-buy-and-unwind the eleven goes 1226 -> 1283, i.e. +57 fielded points, for a net cash outlay of P - 9.731.816. At the current 10.250.000 that is 518.184 for +57 = 9,1k per marginal point; even at the full 10.734.583 ceiling it is 1.002.767 for +57 = 17,6k per marginal point. Set that against the bar this ledger has been applying to everything else on the board - Conte 107k, Kosugi 351k rejected, Demirovic 465k, Robin Koch 184k gross - and Rohr is an order of magnitude better than anything else available. So the ceiling is a hard money constraint and NOT a judgement that the extra premium is unattractive: pay it if it fits. AND PER H5om1wi, RAISING ON A KICKBASE LISTING BUYS WIN PROBABILITY, because these are highest-bid-wins rather than seller's choice - this is the exact configuration in which the Makengo bid was held at +13,03% and lost to +60,76%. ofc 1 now is a snapshot, not a forecast, and the listing sits six hours out, which is the late-contest window that doctrine describes.
